content: The wise man does not expose himself needlessly to danger, since there are few things for which he cares sufficiently; but he is ready, in great crises, to give even his life.
author: Aristotle
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Holding onto anger is like clutching a glowing coal with the intent of throwing it at someone else—you are the one who gets burned. Retaliation only ties you tighter to the person who harmed you.

Aristotle understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Forgiveness and composure are not signs of weakness or giving someone a pass. They are acts of fierce self-preservation, cutting the emotional chain that allows another person's bad behavior to ruin your peace of mind.
reflectionPrompt: What would happen if you met today's stress with steady acceptance rather than resistance?

practicalInsight: When someone triggers your temper today, take three slow breaths before responding. Do not give away your power for the sake of a quick comeback.
